1.Title: Glowing Core
1.Story: Every year when the weather reaches its lowest point, the Phoenix Flower blooms. The tree's soul tells me that when people hang their wishes on its branches, it is not only a time of great joy for the people, but also for the blossoms. The blossoms chatter excitedly about their wishes for Talene. Supposedly, the source of their luminosity, the Celestial, who dwells upon the mountain's peak. - Solise's Botanical Notes, "Phoenix Flower"

2.Title: Fertile Stem
2.Story: I attempted to light the wick of my oil lamp on a fully bloomed Phoenix Flower's Glowing Core stamen, but it went out almost immediately. These tiny specks of light are indeed fragile. Perhaps it's not as effective as just holding the flower in one's hand? The stems are pliable and soft, they can be contorted into all manner of shapes, and if the blossom remains on the stem, it cannot injure your skin. Maybe they'll become the forest's most popular seasonal decoration? Kaz took one on a patrol to light the way, but came back complaining that there wasn't a demon in sight. Could I dare speculate that these flowers might keep those nasty creatures at bay? - Solise's Botanical Notes, "Phoenix Flower"

3.Title: Plume Petal
3.Story:
With Arden's guidance, I sought out clues about the Finch in ancient tomes. In the end, according to what I found in those ancient works, I have divided the Phoenix Flowers into two varieties; Plume Petal, and Twin Wing Petal.
    Experience tells me that fire-related plant life typically has touchable areas that pose no threat of injury when touched, in this case, the brightest and warmest part of the Phoenix Flower. The Plume Petals grow around the outside of the blossom, thick or sparse, there is no consistency. They aren't as uniform as some other plants in the forest, but resemble the slender, vibrant tail plumes of an Obsidian Finch. These petals do not burn and cannot be ignited. I took a number of the blossoms and pressed them into a juice which I then soaked a small cloth in. When I attempted to ignite the cloth, it proved resistant to my efforts. However, it was not able to insulate any heat. Perhaps it is simply a question of fabric choice? I can discuss this point with others... - Solise's Botanical Notes, "Phoenix Flower"

4.Title: Twin Wing Petal
4.Story: Incredible. I've discovered it has unexpected medicinal value. The wing-like petals encircling the stamen have the potential to dispel pyretic toxin and cryo toxin. Hopefully that child that accidentally ate the petals won't experience any ill side effects... Nemora is taking care of her. The Goddess has blessed her, this is probably a divine gift of both the gods and nature. Tomorrow I should go check up on her. - Solise's Botanical Notes, "Phoenix Flower"
